chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Dahqan Ubaydullah, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Wear rings with rubies, for they remove poverty.'
ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of wearing ruby rings according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) recommends wearing rings made of rubies (yawāqīt), linking this adornment to the alleviation of poverty. While Shia scholars often interpret this as a spiritual means of attracting divine sustenance (rizq) or removing the spiritual state of neediness, it also reflects the cultural practice of using precious stones for their perceived barakah. This narration is frequently cited in discussions on the permissibility and virtues of specific gemstones in Islamic tradition.

en.hubeali:
Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Dahqan Ubeydullah, from Al Husayn Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘You should be wearing rings with the emeralds, for these negate the poverty’.
en.sarwar: 4. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Dihqan ‘Ubayd Allah from al-Husayn ibn Khalid who has said the following: “I once heard abu al-Hassan, Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
You must use ruby in the ring; it disallows poverty.’”
